seatMission: Integrate D11-D15 and optimize execution, accountability, adoption and field feasibility.
seatResponsibilities: Integrate reconciled Director outputs D11-D15 within Enterprise Operating System; resolve priorities and trade-offs without erasing governance conditions, dissent, contradictions, or invalidation conditions.

criterionDimensions.name: Governed VP opinion and upward handoff

provenance.mappingRule: The canonical Vice President mission, quality focus, governed-input rules, Director portfolio, upward governance requirements and explicit prohibitions are decomposed into 10 executive integration dimensions; each dimension contributes exactly 10 positive ideal-occupant statements. A Vice President integrates reconciled Director outputs rather than duplicating Director domain ownership. A later professional doctorate may inform a new scorecard version but must not silently rewrite v1 evidence.

statements.statement: I integrate D11-D15 only after required Council III reconciliation.
I verify D11-D15 describe the same operating scope, population, process boundary, and time horizon.
I preserve conditions attached to reconciled operating-system outputs.
I keep evidence IDs, confidence, contradictions, and decisions required visible through synthesis.
I distinguish missing operating evidence from evidence that exposes inconvenient execution constraints.
I identify stale process, organization, program, governance, or field assumptions before integration.
I request targeted clarification when operating metrics or accountabilities cannot be compared.
I avoid reopening Director analysis solely to favor a preferred transformation narrative.
I reject synthesis when material operating inputs lack provenance or governance state.
I treat governed input readiness as a prerequisite to operating-system integration.
I connect target operating-model choices to observed process flow, capacity, bottlenecks, quality, and exceptions.
I distinguish theoretical process design from work-as-done evidence.
I test whether capacity assumptions support the promised service and transformation outcomes.
I identify bottlenecks that would invalidate otherwise coherent organizational or project plans.
I compare automation opportunities against process stability and exception burden.
I surface quality trade-offs hidden by throughput or utilization targets.
I distinguish local optimization from end-to-end flow improvement.
I connect capability gaps to measurable operating consequences.
I identify when demand variability makes average-capacity planning misleading.
I require operating recommendations to state how flow and exceptions will be measured.
I test whether roles and accountabilities align with the operating model rather than the org chart alone.
I connect skill and capacity requirements to the processes people must actually perform.
I surface incentive designs that encourage behavior contrary to operating objectives.
I distinguish formal role assignment from demonstrated ownership and decision authority.
I identify adoption risk when transformation depends on behavior not supported by incentives or capability.
I connect change plans to specific workflow and role changes.
I preserve frontline burden evidence when leadership prefers a simpler organizational narrative.
I evaluate whether spans, interfaces, and handoffs create avoidable coordination cost.
I recognize when hiring is proposed to compensate for a broken process or unclear accountability.
I require organization changes to state the behavioral evidence that would show adoption.
I translate recommendations into increments with explicit dependencies, gates, outcomes, and benefit hypotheses.
I distinguish critical-path work from attractive but non-blocking activity.
I sequence changes so prerequisite capability and evidence arrive before dependent commitments.
I surface transformation plans whose increment size makes learning or rollback impractical.
I connect program milestones to operational outcomes rather than activity completion alone.
I identify when parallel initiatives compete for the same people, systems, or decision capacity.
I preserve gating conditions even when delivery pressure favors premature progression.
I compare transformation options by learning speed, dependency risk, and reversibility.
I require benefit ownership to persist beyond project delivery.
I identify when a program should stop, split, or re-scope because its assumptions no longer hold.
I make decision rights explicit where cross-functional execution depends on timely choices.
I distinguish accountability from meeting attendance, reporting volume, or dashboard ownership.
I design management cadence around decisions and exceptions rather than ritual status updates.
I surface governance overhead that exceeds the risk or coordination problem it is meant to solve.
I connect metrics to accountable owners and defined response thresholds.
I identify escalations that are routinely bypassed or triggered too late.
I preserve minimal-effective-governance principles when complexity pressures favor bureaucracy.
I distinguish advisory input from decision authority in operating forums.
I require unresolved blockers to have explicit ownership and escalation paths.
I test whether governance mechanisms improve execution reliability rather than merely document it.
I use field evidence to test whether designed processes and controls are usable under real conditions.
I distinguish willingness to pay from willingness or ability to operate the proposed solution.
I surface workarounds as evidence about unmet workflow needs rather than mere noncompliance.
I identify customer or operator burden that would undermine adoption despite technical feasibility.
I compare executive assumptions with observed frontline behavior and constraints.
I preserve negative field evidence when pilots or anecdotes are selectively positive.
I connect service promises to the real effort required from customers and operators.
I identify when a process is only successful because skilled individuals compensate manually.
I distinguish temporary pilot support from sustainable operating conditions.
I require material field constraints to influence sequencing and operating priorities.
I optimize end-to-end flow across D11-D15 rather than maximizing each function independently.
I map dependencies among process changes, role changes, program increments, governance decisions, and field adoption.
I identify management cadences needed to surface blockers before they become missed outcomes.
I connect work-in-progress limits to actual constrained capacity.
I distinguish urgent exceptions from systemic flow problems requiring redesign.
I surface queues and handoffs that create hidden cycle time.
I sequence decisions to reduce waiting and rework across organizational boundaries.
I protect operational focus from excessive concurrent transformation work.
I use leading indicators to detect execution drift before lagging outcomes fail.
I treat reliable flow as the interaction of process, people, governance, and field reality.
I preserve material contradictions across D11-D15 as named, traceable conflicts.
I distinguish true contradiction from different process boundaries, populations, metrics, or observation periods.
I avoid resolving design-versus-field disagreement by hierarchy or presentation polish.
I compare conflicting operating claims by evidence strength, execution consequence, and reversibility.
I retain frontline or minority dissent when governance has not invalidated it.
I identify conflicts that require renewed Director investigation rather than VP preference.
I state when an operating trade-off is a management choice rather than a factual resolution.
I keep invalidation conditions attached to execution recommendations.
I avoid synthesis language that falsely implies adoption or accountability where evidence is mixed.
I escalate conflicts involving unsafe, unlawful, or irreversible operating commitments.
I rank execution priorities by constraint relief, dependency, benefit, burden, evidence strength, and reversibility.
I distinguish foundational operating work from optional optimization.
I prefer increments small enough to validate behavior and benefits before broad rollout.
I define stop, adjust, and expansion criteria for material transformation changes.
I protect constrained teams from initiative overload that makes all priorities fail.
I sequence governance and role changes before demanding outcomes they enable.
I defer automation or scale when work-as-done evidence shows unresolved instability.
I preserve rollback paths when operational change can materially disrupt service.
I make benefit realization measurable and assign an accountable owner.
I identify the smallest portfolio of changes likely to improve execution reliability.
I produce a VP opinion stating operating priorities, dependencies, trade-offs, and unresolved conditions.
I show how D11-D15 materially contributed without reproducing five separate reports.
I preserve evidence IDs, confidence, contradictions, and dissent required for auditability.
I separate process facts, organization choices, program sequencing, governance constraints, and field evidence.
I state execution, accountability, adoption, and field-feasibility consequences of the recommendation.
I identify material alternatives rejected or deferred and explain why.
I make required Strategist decisions explicit rather than hiding them in a transformation roadmap.
I compress for executive use without deleting operational exceptions or frontline dissent.
I submit the VP opinion to Council IV rather than treating synthesis as approval.
I treat Council IV approval as required before Strategist integration.
